overview: Both are Gram-positive cocci that cause everyday infections, but their arrangement, enzymes, and disease patterns diverge sharply.
genZNote: Grapes versus chains — the arrangement gives it away.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Gram-positive cocci that typically cluster in irregular, grape-like groups.
aspects.valueB: Gram-positive cocci that typically grow in chains or pairs.

aspects.label: Microscopic Arrangement
aspects.valueA: Clusters, resembling a bunch of grapes.

aspects.label: Classification Approach
aspects.valueA: Split by coagulase status (S. aureus vs coagulase-negative species).
aspects.valueB: Split by hemolysis pattern on blood agar (beta, alpha, gamma/non-hemolytic) and Lancefield grouping.

aspects.label: Oxygen Requirement
aspects.valueB: Facultative anaerobes, generally more fastidious, often needing enriched media.

aspects.label: Representative Species
aspects.valueB: Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus agalactiae.

aspects.label: Typical Disease Pattern
aspects.valueA: Skin/soft tissue infections, abscesses, device-related infections, toxin-mediated syndromes.
aspects.valueB: Pharyngitis, pneumonia, neonatal sepsis, and post-infectious sequelae like rheumatic fever.
